REPORT FOR ACTION 
Transit Priority Measures to Support the 505 Dundas 
6-Minute Network 
Date: November 10, 2025 
To: Toronto and East York Community Council 
From: Director, Congestion and Network Management, Transportation Services 
Wards: 4 – Parkdale-High Park, 9 – Davenport, 13 – Toronto Centre 
SUMMARY 
Transportation Services is requesting approval, on behalf of the Toronto Transit 
Commission (TTC), to install transit priority measures (TPMs) to support 6-minute 
headways on the 505 Dundas streetcar route from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily, with these 
service improvements to 6-minute headways beginning in November 2025. If approved, 
the TPMs to support the 6-minute headways would be implemented January 2026. 
The proposed changes aim to benefit the passengers using the 505 Dundas route, who 
currently total over 205,000 per week. 
The purpose of this report is to recommend a suite of TPMs to help improve the speed 
and reliability of the 505 Dundas route and alleviate the risk of increased bunching and 
gapping associated with moving to a more frequent headway. The proposed changes 
span Dundas Street West between Bloor Street West (near Dundas West Station) and 
Dovercourt Road; and Dundas Street East between Yonge Street and Parliament 
Street. The changes include expanding ‘No Stopping’ coverage of the AM and PM peak 
periods on weekdays, as well as new and expanded left-turn restrictions on Dundas 
Street and Wellesley Street. 
The change to curbside regulations proposed in this report is to have ‘No Stopping’ 
coverage in both the AM and PM peak periods on both sides of the street, where it is 
currently only AM or PM. The hours for the new ‘No Stopping’ period reflect the hours 
used on the opposite side of the street. This would make the ‘No Stopping’ match for 
both sides of the road for both the AM and PM peak periods, improving consistency for 
the restrictions along the corridor while improving traffic flow for the added periods. For 
example, if the north side of Dundas Street West has ‘No Stopping’ from 7 a.m. to 9 
a.m., Mon. to Fri., and the south side has ‘No Stopping’ from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m., Mon. to

Fri., both sides of Dundas Street West are proposed to have ‘No Stopping’ from 7 a.m. 
to 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. to 6 p.m., Mon. to Fri. 
The changes proposed in this report only span a portion of the 505 Dundas route – 
broader changes for the entire corridor are still being investigated and will be the subject 
of a future report. The TTC will also work with the City to monitor the impacts of the 
proposed changes to determine if the extents and the periods need to be changed. 
The changes proposed in this report impact the AM and PM peak periods for ‘No 
Stopping’ restrictions on weekdays while the left-turn restrictions impact different 
periods depending on the location. Based on 2025 travel time data, there are additional 
time periods during the week that have slow speeds on the 505 Dundas route, such as 
Saturday and Sunday afternoons. The TTC, in partnership with Transportation Services, 
will continue to engage with customers, local Councillors, residents, and BIAs along the 
505 Dundas route on more comprehensive TPMs that will aim to improve the speed and 
reliability of transit. 
The recommendations in this report support the initiative to improve transit speed and 
reliability, as outlined in the Congestion Management Plan. The proposed TPMs support 
the designation of Dundas Street East and West in the area covered by this report as a 
Priority Roadway for transit improvement, as identified in the RapidTO: Surface Transit 
Network Plan approved by City Council in February 2024. 
As TTC operates transit service on Dundas Street East and Dundas Street West, City 
Council approval of this report is required. 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
The Director, Congestion and Network Management, Transportation Services 
recommends that: 
1. City Council authorize amendments to parking and traffic regulations as set out in 
Attachment 1, to take effect from January 1, 2026. 
2. City Council direct the General Manager, Transportation Services, in consultation 
with the Chief Executive Officer, Toronto Transit Commission, to collect traffic 
and transit data, monitor the performance of the transit priority measures, subject 
to data availability. 
FINANCIAL IMPACT 
Transportation Services has consulted with Toronto Parking Authority (TPA), who 
assessed that the potential financial impact of lost revenue and operating expenses will 
be approximately $245,000 in the first year and $239,000 in subsequent years (HST

excluded). The estimated cost to implement the curbside and turning regulations is 
$130,000 (pre-HST), which will be funded from the TTC’s 2025-2034 Capital Budget 
and Plan. 
DECISION HISTORY 
The Mayor’s 2025 Proposed Operating Budget was approved with amendments by City 
Council, at its meeting on February 11, 2025. The approved 2025 Operating Budget 
(2025 Budget Notes – Toronto Transit Commission) includes funding to advance the 
implementation of 6-minute or better service from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., 7 days a week on 
505 Dundas, 512 St. Clair, and 511 Bathurst streetcar routes. 
Agenda Item History – 2025.MPB27.1 
City Council, at its meeting on June 25 and 26, 2025, adopted Item TE23.50 entitled 
“Parking and Traffic Amendments – Dundas Street West – Findings Report on Pilot 
Initiative”. This motion made permanent the temporary changes to parking and traffic 
regulations that were originally introduced to improve transit service along Dundas 
Street West between Spadina Avenue and McCaul Street during the closure of the 510 
Spadina streetcar right-of-way from June 2024 to March 2025. As part of these 
changes, TTC travel times were observed to improve up to 7% on weekdays and 6% on 
weekends in the eastbound direction, and up to 21% on weekdays and 10% on 
weekends in the westbound direction.

COMMENTS 
Background 
The 505 Dundas currently connects Broadview Station and Dundas West Station on 
Line 2 Bloor-Danforth via Broadview Avenue, Dundas Street East, and Dundas Street 
West. The route has a round-trip distance of 21.7 kilometers. 
Travel times on the route vary considerably by time period. Based on 75th percentile 
travel times as of Summer 2025, end-to-end runtimes range from 52 minutes to 86 
minutes depending on direction and time period. The average speeds across the route 
range from 8 km/hr to 12 km/hr depending on direction and time period, with speeds 
dropping to as low as 4 km/hr on some segments of the route. The goal of the TPMs 
associated with the implementation of 6-minute headways on the 505 Dundas streetcar 
are to increase reliability and improve speeds during historically slower time periods 
along the route. 
In May 2024, temporary traffic and parking amendments were made on Dundas Street 
West between Spadina Avenue and McCaul Street to enhance transit service during 
construction on Spadina Avenue. As part of these amendments, TTC travel times were 
observed to improve up to 7% on weekdays and 6% on weekends in the eastbound

direction, and up to 21% on weekdays and 10% on weekends in the westbound 
direction. The changes were made permanent in June 2025 (2025.TE23.50). The TPMs 
proposed in this report are smaller-scale, impacting the AM and PM peak periods for 
‘No Stopping’ restrictions on weekdays while the left-turn restrictions impact different 
periods depending on the location. The TPMs follow the same principles of addressing 
slower speeds and improving reliability through restricting curbside use and freeing up 
an additional lane of traffic.

Transit Priority Measures 
The proposed TPMs were developed by focusing on parking and traffic regulatory 
prohibitions during the AM and PM peak periods on weekdays. These measures aim to 
improve the speed and reliability of the 505 Dundas streetcar in the peak periods. 
Dundas Street East and West in the area covered by this report are included in the 
RapidTO: Surface Transit Network Plan as Priority Roadways for transit improvement. 
The TPMs proposed in this report represent low-infrastructure improvements that will 
provide improved transit service without significant disruptions to general traffic flow. 
Stopping Restrictions 
Parking adjacent to a streetcar lane results in more general traffic occupying the same 
lane as the streetcar and increases weaving of traffic. Additionally, when vehicles 
complete a parking manoeuvre there can be a delay to streetcars, and general traffic, 
until the vehicle is fully parked. ‘No Parking’ restrictions permit loading/unloading 
activity, meaning that while ‘No Parking’ restrictions are in effect, delivery vehicles can 
use the curbside lane while actively engaged in loading and unloading of the delivery. In 
contrast, ‘No Stopping’ restrictions generally do not permit motorists to stop for any 
reason except to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a 
police officer, traffic control sign or signal (City of Toronto Parking Regulations). 
Dundas Street East and Dundas Street West currently support one streetcar route, the 
505 Dundas, which currently runs every 10 minutes and will be increased to every 6 
minutes from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily starting in November 2025. Due to the high number 
of streetcars that will be utilizing Dundas Street East and Dundas Street West as part of 
the long-term increase in frequency of the 505 Dundas, the existing time-of-day 
restrictions need to be expanded to support reliability of service. 
The changes to curbside regulations only target sections of Dundas Street West and 
Dundas Street East where there are ‘No Stopping’ restrictions in only one peak period 
from Monday to Friday, on each side of the street. In these sections, the curbside 
regulations will be updated so each side of the street has ‘No Stopping’ in both peak 
periods, from Monday to Friday. This would make the ‘No Stopping’ restrictions match 
for both sides of the road for both the AM and PM peak periods, improving consistency

Impacts on General Purpose Traffic 
Most of the impact of the TPMs on general traffic is expected to be positive; an increase 
in ‘No Stopping’ zones means that the existing lanes will have more capacity in 
additional time periods. An increase in left-turn restrictions means that existing 
intersections will have more throughput capacity, due to green time for through traffic 
not being lost by a left-turning vehicle blocking the lane with minimal impact on access 
to neighbourhood roads. It is challenging to quantify the expected benefit, but beyond 
an “extra” lane being available, the reduction in merging activity for vehicles traveling 
along the curb lane reduces localized traffic congestion as well as an elimination of 
parking maneuvers.

Consultation 
As part of implementing the TPMs, TTC has engaged with local Councillors and BIAs to 
communicate the proposed changes and obtain feedback. These conversations are on-
going and will continue before and after implementation, taking into account the 
monitoring discussed in the next section. For local residents and businesses, mailers 
will be sent out to communicate the changes to the parking restrictions along Dundas 
Street and nearby local streets. Conversations with the Councillors, including 
Councillors in adjacent wards will continue, as TTC and Transportation Services monitor 
the effectiveness of the propose TPMs, to determine the need for future TPMs. 
Monitoring 
Transportation Services and the TTC will monitor traffic and transit data after installing 
the TPMs on the affected roadways. This will include: 
• Monitoring the on-street operations to optimize signal timings/operating 
strategies as required. 
• Monitoring ridership to maintain acceptable headways/service reliability. 
• Monitoring safety metrics to identify and resolve issues as needed. 
The main metrics monitored will be: 
• Motor Vehicle Travel Times: changes in motor vehicle travel times (average, 95th 
percentile, etc.) during defined periods. 
• Transit Travel Time: observed travel times (average, 85th percentile, etc.) during 
defined periods.
